findings.title: Illicit gain enters as appetite
findings.claim: The focus phrase places illicit gain inside an image of consumption: the gain is eaten, and the act of taking it can be perceived as an intake that strips the consumer's integrity and leaves appetite unsatisfied.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier أكّالون meets the adjacent السحت, activating the supplied wealth-consumption and illicit-gain facets; the same focus surface also carries the sourced stripping and unsated-appetite images. The immediate 5:41 pattern of bent wording and selective taking supplies the macro pressure that turns the phrase from a pair of accusations into a bodily corruption image.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the text uses eating language for corrupt gain: the gain is not only possessed or exchanged, it enters the person and is pictured as removing what should remain intact while appetite continues.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains that they consume forbidden gain. The stripping and hunger elements are bounded analogical images; the hungry-person facet is not asserted as the grammatical denotation of السحت, and the finding does not claim a literal diagnosis of digestion.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel support and exact focus carriers support the relation, while the stripping and unsated-appetite facets are reframed or analogical rather than the focus phrase's primary lexical denotation.

epistemic.reason: The HFT coordinates and focus returns are complete, but the affective-to-judicial synthesis is attributed and the source identity is legacy-unbound.
